title_en: 'Life is too brief to leave this planet'
title_zh: 生命太短暂，不能离开这个星球

paragraphs.en: For centuries, Mars has been seen as a potential place for future human settlements. But long-duration space travel comes with serious risks to astronauts' health , including those resulting from cosmic radiation and the effects of microgravity .
paragraphs.zh: 几个世纪以来，火星一直被视为未来人类定居的潜在地点。但长时间的太空旅行会给宇航员的健康带来严重风险，包括宇宙辐射和微重力的影响。

paragraphs.en: A new study found that rats that were exposed to radiation similar to what astronauts might encounter during a Mars mission developed more scar tissue around their hearts' small blood vessels compared with a control group. Although the findings haven't been validated in humans, the results contribute to growing concerns about the potential effects of long-haul space missions on astronauts' health.
paragraphs.zh: 一项新的研究发现，与对照组相比，暴露在类似于宇航员在火星任务中可能遇到的辐射下的老鼠，心脏小血管周围的疤痕组织更多。尽管这一发现尚未在人类身上得到验证，但这一结果引发了人们对长途太空任务对宇航员健康的潜在影响的担忧。

paragraphs.en: Given these new findings, Live Science asked its readers whether they'd travel to the Red Planet , despite these potential health risks. Over 240 readers weighed in, with 65% picking "No, I don't think the risks are worth it."
paragraphs.zh: 鉴于这些新发现，《生活科学》杂志询问读者，尽管存在这些潜在的健康风险，他们是否会去火星旅行。超过240名读者参与了讨论，65%的人选择了“不，我认为不值得冒险。”

paragraphs.en: Interestingly enough, the comments reflect a slightly different trend. One reader wrote, "Any pioneers who travel to Mars will be facing the prospect of death and never coming back. Even if they make it back, there are any number of health issues that could come up. These risks have not stopped people from exploring throughout human history. The bigger question is who to send?"
paragraphs.zh: 有趣的是，这些评论反映了一种略有不同的趋势。一位读者写道：“任何前往火星的先驱者都将面临死亡的前景，永远不会回来。即使他们回来了，也会出现很多健康问题。纵观人类历史，这些风险并没有阻止人们进行探索。更大的问题是派谁去？”

paragraphs.en: Other commenters echoed this sentiment, with another reader posting, "Explorers in the past have always been exposed to unusual risks; without the risk takers we would still believe the world is flat ."
paragraphs.zh: 其他评论者也表达了同样的观点，另一位读者写道：“过去的探险家总是面临着不寻常的风险；如果没有冒险者，我们仍然会认为地球是平的。”

paragraphs.en: Beyond the feelings that Mars will be explored anyway, despite the health risks, other commenters highlighted the cost of these missions, with one reader stating, "Sending flesh water balloons to Mars is ridiculous. For the cost of one human on Mars, we could literally probe the entire solar system and map/sample/rove every planet and every major Moon."
paragraphs.zh: 除了感觉无论如何都会探索火星，尽管存在健康风险，其他评论者强调了这些任务的成本，一位读者说： “将血肉水球送到火星是荒谬的。对于一个人在火星上的成本，我们可以从字面上探测整个太阳系，并绘制/采样/漫游每个行星和每个主要月球。“

paragraphs.en: Others highlighted the mental and emotional cost of a trip to Mars. "As a devoted sci-fi fan for decades, I always wished I could go into space," another reader noted. "Now that I am 77 years old, I realize I would miss the outdoors. The wind and trees, the birdsong and sweet grass under my feet would be a devastating loss. Let the brave explorers go instead. Life is too brief to leave this planet for the uncertainty and dangers of space travel."
paragraphs.zh: 其他人则强调了火星之旅的精神和情感代价。另一位读者指出： “几十年来，作为一名忠实的科幻迷，我一直希望能够进入太空。” “现在我已经77岁了，我意识到我会想念户外活动。风和树木，我脚下的鸟鸣声和甜美的草地将是毁灭性的损失。让勇敢的探险家走吧。生命太短暂，不能因为太空旅行的不确定性和危险而离开这个星球。”

paragraphs.en: Kenna Hughes-Castleberry is the Content Manager at Live Science. Formerly, she was the Content Manager at Space.com and before that the Science Communicator at JILA, a physics research institute. Kenna is also a book author, with her upcoming book 'Octopus X' scheduled for release in spring of 2027. Her beats include physics, health, environmental science, technology, AI, animal intelligence, corvids, and cephalopods.
paragraphs.zh: Kenna Hughes-Castleberry是Live Science的内容经理。之前，她是Space.com的内容经理，之前是物理研究所JILA的科学传播者。肯娜也是一位书籍作者，她即将出版的书《章鱼X》计划于2027年春季发行。她的节拍包括物理、健康、环境科学、技术、人工智能、动物智能、corvids和头足类动物。
